site_name: Meta Huntsville data center, North Huntsville Industrial Park
serving_utility: Tennessee Valley Authority, served directly (Meta also has a small contract with Huntsville Utilities for light auxiliary power)
utility_evidence_period: a statement by Meta's community development regional manager on a media tour of 21 October 2026, published 25 October 2026; no page dates when direct service began
notes: Reopened at Joe's request (session 8). AL.com (Scott Turner), republished by Yahoo, 25 October 2026: 'Thornton said the facility buys its electricity directly from the Tennessee Valley Authority, although it does have a small contract with Huntsville Utilities for light auxiliary power. "It's a small thing compared to the TVA direct serve," Thornton said.' WAFF, 22 October 2026: 'Thornton said the facility receives its power through the Tennessee Valley Authority.' A blog's account of the same tour says the same. Against it: the page this site was first verified on, Alabama Political Reporter, 27 August 2026, a reporter's sentence with no source: the campus 'receives power through Huntsville Utilities, a TVA local power company'. Under D-48 the operator's named statement governs at medium and the site is flagged. The sales check of D-45 points the same way: Meta reports 866 GWh here for 2024 and the City of Huntsville's non-residential sales did not rise. The auxiliary contract with Huntsville Utilities is not quantified on any page and carries no load here. An Axios Huntsville article of 22 October 2026 said to cover the same point refused the request twice and was not obtained. All three pages opened by the session model.

Territory listing, not a statement about the site (D-48). Eversource's 'Communities we serve' page lists NEEDHAM under 'Massachusetts - Electric'. Nothing on file says a second utility delivers in Needham. The national territory map had put this building on the Town of Braintree's municipal utility, which is two towns away. Opened by the session model.

Territory listing, not a statement about the site (D-48). Eversource's 'Communities we serve' page lists NEEDHAM under 'Massachusetts - Electric'. Confirms the utility the map already gave this building. Opened by the session model.

site_name: Congruity360 data center, 456 Bedford St, Fall River
utility_evidence_period: release of 26 July 2017; the city's page on who delivers is undated, read 2026-11-14
notes: Congruity360's own release, dateline Fall River, 26 July 2017: the company accepted 'energy efficiency rebate funds from National Grid', presented by a National Grid account manager 'during a ceremony held at Congruity 360's data center'. It gives no street address. The City of Fall River's community electricity page (https://www.fallriverma.gov/residents/fall_river_community_electricity_aggregation_program.php): 'National Grid continues to deliver electricity, repair poles and outages'. The national territory map had put this site on the Town of North Attleborough's municipal utility. Both pages opened by the session model.

utility_evidence_kind: local map with a utility page
utility_evidence_period: Evergy release of 29 September 2023; map record last modified July 2021, queried 2026-11-14
notes: Local map with a utility page (D-48). Johnson County's 'Electric Service Areas' layer, served from the City of Olathe's map server (https://arcgis.olatheks.org/arcgis/rest/services/EnerGov/EnerGov_display_map/FeatureServer/39; layer described as 'Electric Company Service Area Boundaries', record last modified July 2021), returns ProviderName 'Evergy, Kansas Metro' at this site's coordinates; queried by the session model on 2026-11-14. Evergy's own release of 29 September 2023 says: 'For Evergy Kansas Metro, which includes Lenexa, Overland Park and other communities near the Kansas City metro area'. The City of Lenexa's utilities page lists 'Power: Evergy' (https://www.lenexa.com/Your-Residence/Trash-Utilities/Utilities, undated, read 2026-11-14). Neither page is about this site. The national territory map had put it on the Kansas City, Kansas Board of Public Utilities, which the local layer does not show in Johnson County at all. Found by a Sonnet 5.5 lookup; every page opened by the session model.

site_name: CoreWeave at Core Scientific's Denton campus
utility_evidence_period: as of 31 December 2025 (Core Scientific's annual report for 2025)
notes: Core Scientific's annual report for 2025, table of 'gross utility power capacity in MW by facility location and electric utility provider as of December 31, 2025': 'Denton Municipal Electric 394 Dallas-Denton, Texas'. The filing does not name CoreWeave at Denton; that the Epoch row is Core Scientific's Denton campus is Epoch's, hence medium. Confirms the utility the map gave. Opened by the session model.

utility_evidence_period: developer's release of 26 November 2018, about a building to be completed in summer 2019
notes: KDC, the developer, 26 November 2018, of the building 'to be located at 1510 E. Lookout Drive': 'It contains an onsite electrical substation that is owned and maintained by ONCOR.' The national territory map had put it on Fannin County Electric Cooperative. An ERCOT wires company, so the site carries no load on a panel utility (D-4). Opened by the session model.

utility_evidence_period: a press tour of 24 September 2026; the article does not date the substation's transfer
notes: San Antonio Report (Shari Biediger), on a press tour of CyrusOne's Omicron Drive campus in the Texas Research Park on 24 September 2026: 'From the CyrusOne data center, there's a clear view of the electrical substation that the company built, then transferred to CPS Energy, to serve its facilities and the surrounding neighborhoods.' About the campus, not this street number, hence medium. The national territory map had put it on Guadalupe Valley Electric Cooperative. Opened by the session model.
